headline: Sales rise on pass-through pricing, but profit slips
summary_short: Net sales rose to $1.64 billion (+6.8% y/y, +5.3% q/q) on the contractual pass-through of higher raw material costs across all three segments, while GAAP net income fell to $75.8 million (-14.8% y/y) as consolidated EBIT declined to $151.0 million from $167.5 million and the effective tax rate rose to 28.1% from 25.6%.
summary_long: Sales growth was a pass-through story: all segments raised prices to recover higher raw material costs, led by Metal Containers (+13% sales) on roughly flat volume. EBIT fell to $151.0M from $167.5M as less-favorable price/cost in Metal Containers and Dispensing & Specialty Closures, higher corporate expense, and rationalization charges outweighed sales growth. GAAP diluted EPS fell to $0.72 from $0.83 on the lower EBIT and a higher tax rate (28.1% vs 25.6%); adjusted diluted EPS was roughly flat at $0.98 vs $1.01. Cash fell to $351.5M from $1,080.7M at year-end on debt paydown and working-capital build. Company confirmed FY2026 adjusted EPS guidance ($3.73-$3.93) and FCF guidance (~$450M), and gave Q3 2026 adjusted EPS guidance of $1.21-$1.31.

drivers.explanation: Sales grew entirely on contractual raw-material cost pass-through, not volume; GAAP profit fell y/y on less-favorable segment price/cost and a higher tax rate, while adjusted EPS was roughly flat ($0.98 vs $1.01).

Increase driven by the contractual pass-through of higher raw material and manufacturing costs, most visibly in Metal Containers (+13% sales); company-wide volumes were comparable to flat y/y, not a demand story.

Not broken out separately at the gross-profit line; the closest disclosed cause is segment EBIT commentary citing less favorable price/cost in Metal Containers and Dispensing & Specialty Closures, partly offset by favorable price/cost in Custom Containers.

EBIT fell to $151.0M from $167.5M on less favorable price/cost in Metal Containers and Dispensing & Specialty Closures plus higher corporate expense and rationalization charges, partially offset by slightly lower interest expense.
Tracks the EBIT decline plus a higher effective tax rate (28.1% vs 25.6% in Q2 2025); interest expense was modestly lower y/y.
Tracks the net income decline; diluted share count was roughly flat (105.8M vs 107.3M), so it is not a meaningful offset.

Cash fell from the $1,080.7M 2025 year-end balance (and -19.3% q/q) as operating cash flow was consumed by a receivables/inventory working-capital build and $146.7M of H1 capex, partly offset by $548.2M of net new borrowings; cash still rose y/y versus Q2 2025.
Y/y increase reflects the $548.2M of net borrowings and other financing activity disclosed in the H1 2026 cash-flow statement; the release does not break out use of proceeds beyond that.
Consistent with retained-earnings growth from six-month net income of $138.8M against $45.1M of dividends paid; not a separately stated cause in the release.
